newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends unchanged in nervous trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends unchanged in nervous trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's gold market ended unchanged on Friday from the New York close Thursday after nervous two-way trade, gold dealers and traders said.
Attempts to push the market down below $379 by gold dealers in morning trade failed as gold held near $380 per ounce, gold traders said.

Bullion saw good professional buying interest at around $380.50 per ounce, but when prices edged up to $380.60/90, selling interest resumed and the market sank back to around $380.20/50 where it remained, gold sources said.
Small volumes of profit-taking from European players were seen in afternoon trade as the market remained jittery, traders said.
"Sentiment is still a bit nervous," said the chief bullion dealer at an international bank, adding that U.S.-based funds could try and cover short positions.
The outlook for gold prices remained mixed, with some saying gold would hold at $380 and others seeing a further drop.
Bullion ended at US$380.10/60 an ounce Friday against New York's US$380.10/50 close on Thursday.
Local gold ended HK$7 higher at HK$3,501 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -5 on Friday from its previous fix at -6.
Physical trade remained sluggish as buyers remained largely sidelined, industry sources said. BULLION - Hong Kong midday - US$380.20/70 Hong Kong open - US$380.40/90
